An awesome small parkour game that is basically everything I wanted for years now. If you are one of the maybe 5 people to share my experience of playing every small game involving parkour or even stuff like parkour mods in GTA San Andreas, this is finally the game to finally deliver on the Parkour Sandbox experience. If you ever played Free Running, it is a more refined and fun focused version of that game.
Don't expect a grand story mode or tons of singleplayer content, there are very beautiful maps with varied environments and challenges, after which you find your own lines to run either for speed or for trick score. That or just be like me and try to land one ridiculous gap trick for an hour. Multiplayer is also quick, easy and good! I especially like the tag mode.

I got the game early in its development and I am glad that the solo dev delivered on all his promises and is also going beyond with his post launch support.

The Soundtrack is also fantastic and has been stuck in my head! Great Tracks that I instantly recognize and mentally connect to the game.

I couldn't even ask for much more if I tried, besides maybe more tricks? I was spoiled by all the combinations you could do with Free Runnings Trick buffer system that allowed for deep lists of moves, R&A is already pretty much maximizing it's available buttons so I'm not disappointed if more Tricks won't happen.


A fun product in early access, a finished product outside of early access in a reasonable time, this is one of the great examples of Indie Early Access done right. The final asking price is also fair, I got a solid discount as an Early Access player but i'd gladly pay the full asking price again and I wish the best to the dev. Hope you continue with more games of this quality even if it leaves the realm of parkour!

Rooftops and Alleys is an amazing game! Easy to learn but hard to master. There are 6 different unique maps (5 when this review was written but 6 when 1.0 releases) with a variety of different obstacles that you can do tricks on. The game teaches you some moves but you also get to experiment learning new moves and combos. Time trials help keep you engaged during while you play and give you a sense of accomplishment when you finally get the gold medal. Time trials also make you want to come back to beat your highscore again and again. Additionally, there are multiplayer features and gamemodes. The current gamemodes are tag and trick battle, they offer unique and fun experiences which are fun with friends or others online (more negatives mentioned later). The main multiplayer feature is a leaderboard on time trials, this keeps you playing just to beat one of your friends so you can prove that your better.

BUT, every game has its flaws. Although each map offers a different experience, after you explore each one, you might find it boring revisiting the old ones (of course it depends what type of person you are). Furthermore, the maps are fairly small, I belive that instead of focusing about size, the maps are focused on specific areas where players can freerun and combine lots of trick together. I personally like fully exploring all the maps and find it fun finding the small details scattered around the map. There is one problem with the multiplayer gamemode, if you don't have friends willing to play the game/buy the game, then it can be hard to get into a multiplayer game because there aren't many other solo people that also want to play multiplayer.

In conclusion, if you are looking for a game with the most realism, just wait for STORROR Parkour Pro to release (in about 6-12 months from when this review is written). Rooftops and Alleys is a great game where you can explore around unique maps doing different tricks. It keeps you coming back to beat time trial and learn combos. The game has realistic aspects but also less realistic things to make the game more fun. KEEP IN MIND, this game is made by a SOLO DEVELOPER, they are doing their best developing the game.

I forgot to mention this earlier, but the game has an AMAZING music soundtrack (the developer was previously a dj). The music gives the game a very unique vibe and overall enhances the experience.

Rooftops & Alleys: The Parkour Game’s ethos is perfectly described by its own subtitle. This is quite simply, “The Parkour Game.” For decades, we’ve had many big-budget open-world titles implementing freerunning into their exploration, like Assassin’s Creed or Dying Light. Parkour in these games feels satisfying, but the controls are simplified as it’s just another tool in games with very broad focuses. When you get a game more holistically focused on parkour, such as Mirror’s Edge, it’s usually an extremely fast-paced experience that wraps up after a few hours.

Rooftops & Alleys breaks these trends by focusing on an elaborate freerunning system whilst also providing total player freedom. Whether you want swift, efficient movement or ridiculously elaborate displays of style, Rooftops & Alleys has you covered.

But how much can an excellent parkour system carry a full game? Well, if it’s fun enough, I’d say it absolutely can, but Rooftops & Alleys stumbles just often enough to make enjoying the game a constant battle. Despite an excellent core, issues across its movement systems and empty levels always seemed to limit its potential. How much these issues will bother you will come down to personal experience. When Rooftops & Alleys is at its best, it’s an amazing experience. Unfortunately, it’s rarely at its best.

This is so far a game that is under cooked. It is a collection of maps and mechanics that do work in conjunction with each other; there is no story, there is no progression, but there are some good vibes. It is a good "blow off some steam game." 
However, in a game where intrinsic motivation is the fundamental propellant to play, inconsistency and jank become more and more difficult to forgive. Jumping up to a 3 foot tall concrete wall is the greatest danger to free flow. 
Two and a half of the face buttons are dedicated to doing tricks that don't really do it for me. 
This is not a game where you make you're own fun by working within a movement sandbox; you run forward with RT, hope that the jump button works as it should, and then hold LT to grab a wall.
There is no back eject meaning close walls cannot be scaled. 
Ledges protruding from walls don't like to be grabbed.
Now, if i kept going all would be making a bug list and be that as it may there are some flaws. with how things feel to pull off.
If you want a good parkour indie game with high potential, this is for you.
If you want a parkour game that provides extrinsic and intrinsic motivation for it's game play, feels good to pull off, and has a wider move set; play AC Unity.

Great game, real fun. I have a few things, but let it be known I've only played on PC, so I'm only speaking for that control scheme:

1: Camera should be more maneuverable mid-air.

I understand the camera influencing movement, but movement influencing the camera, while it looks smoother, is really painful for precise lines. This is mostly in reference to wall ejecting/wallrunning, where it feels like I have little to no control while executing them quickly in a row.

2: Trick sensitivity needs to be increased.

Its happened too many times now when I go to launch off a short wall or a stack of pallets that my character does a 360 gainer out of nowhere even though I don't even move my mouse at all. I do like the whole "button hold + directional input" formula for tricks, but the sensitivity definitely needs to be increased. I see happening to other people in multiplayer as well, so I'm sure I'm not alone on this. Just increasing it in general or a trick sensitivity slider for it in the settings would be great.

3: Movement and responses need to be snappier.

When I turn around, it's like I'm rotating around a fixed point even if the only inputs I'm making are forwards and backwards. This makes it really hard to reposition my character while it's standing on a ledge or beam because half the time that small rotation will just make you fall off. A suggestion I have is that if you're sprinting and suddenly start hold S, the character should skid to a stop and then start running in the opposite direction. The skid distance should be determined on your speed and if you're walking, it's just a quick turn. One that doesn't rotate you anyway.

I think its a really good idea, executed almost perfectly. Good emphasis on flow, amazing looking tricks, while also having a clear respect for technical movement. The game isn't all just backflips and roof gaps, there's actual meaningful movement and the maps encourage you to look for places to use it. Even with all these complaints I still really enjoy the gameplay. It's met my expectations visually and mechanically, with these three things being the only real exceptions.

I was blown away by how intuitive the parkour mechanics are. The game really gives you a ton of choice to pull off specific moves and challenges that you actually feel an accomplishment for completing. This truly is THE parkour game. It's honestly surprising that it took this long before we got a free roam, realistic parkour simulator that's actually good. Movement strikes a balance between realism and snappiness that feels really good. It's difficult to get to grips with, and it's even harder to master, but once you do it ends up feeling extremely satisfying, and you look really cool too. It's much harder than something like Bomb Rush Cyberfunk, but not as difficult as Tony Hawk. It's an incredibly chill game despite the difficulty, and it's really fun just running around while listening to your favorite music (though the ingame music is quite good as well). All of the 6 current maps are very well designed and fun to move around in, and the challenges are tough but fair and get easier as you get better. I enjoy that all of the cosmetics are tied to completing challenges and finding pigeons, making it so that the clothes you wear actually reflect how good you are at the game, kinda like certain Spartan armors in older Halo games.

I only played solo. There's certainly enough content for the price, though I do wish there was even more. Besides time trials and trick challenges, there's not much else to do besides free roam, and each map only has one collectable encouraging exploration (the pigeon). There's enough challenges to keep you busy for a while, but once you complete them all there's nothing left besides free roam and multiplayer. Hopefully future updates will add more maps, more activities, and more features (leaderboards and mod support would be especially welcome). I would love to keep playing this game forever, I just need an excuse to.

Now that the game has left early access, I can go into the love and hate relationship I've had with this game for a good while now.

PROS:
- The parkour feels realistic while remaining fluid.
- The sound design is great. The sound of your clothes shuffling as you parkour really adds to the game.
- Adrenaline is very well designed. A great risk = reward system that especially excels in time trials.
- The tricks are really cool looking.
- The maps, while not big, provide a lot to play around with.
- The pigeon is a great way to provide the player with easy transportation.
- Lots of customization options which make the game feel more personalized. 

CONS:
- Different tricks require flicking your mouse in different directions. Sometimes feels incredibly inconsistent.
- There is no way to change your keybinds.
- Trick rush is a terrible gamemode. Point farming is not fun.
- First person mode is still nauseating even with the default settings. Needs an overhaul.

Overall, a pretty great game for parkour enthusiasts.

This game is my definitive parkour game, taking the spot from the Mirror's Edge series, both fantastic games in their own regard. For me, this truly captures what it feels like to be a parkour/free-running practitioner. Seemingly borrowing design philosophy from the Skate games in regards to how detailed the mechanics are for parkour specifically, the game definitely has a learning curve, but once it clicks it becomes an astoundingly in-depth parkour experience. 

The gameplay is phenomenal and easily the highlight of the game. Every button movement of the stick is tied to movement in some way, creating a parkour system that is far more in-depth than any other of its peers, even ones dedicated to it like Mirror's Edge. The tricking system feels cool and the game encourages you to blend both disciplines of parkour, which focuses on efficient movement and freerunning, focusing on creativity and expression, to perform optimally in the many challenges on the map. That being said, this is all optional buy in, so players more dedicated to performing flips and tricks over efficiency can play their way at no penalty and vice versa for efficiency focused players like myself. The maps are all well crafted for the purposes of verticality and flow and I am excited to see what is added in the future. 

A big part of why I enjoy the game is how it makes me feel. This is coming not just from a gamer but from someone who practices parkour myself. I was out with an injury that stopped me from training and found this game. As I went through the settings I found realistic camera mode for first person and never looked back. Using this setting, it felt exactly as I would feel in a training session and is a feeling I cherish even to this day. Not only did this get me through the injury period but it also gave me a drive to return to training, all this because of the care that went into how accurately this realistic first person camera mode worked. Needless to say, the game truly captures how it feels to be a traceur. 

The graphics are simple but do the job, being a cell shaded style that gives the game it's own personality. Combined with the soundtrack, it creates a very cool atmosphere that lends itself well to just unwinding as you run around the map in your own way. That being said, I do personally love throwing on the Mirror's Edge soundtrack and reliving the days of when Mirror's Edge Catalyst had servers and still worked. 

Perhaps my only gripe being the progression system, unlocks are locked behind feathers that you now collect from using challenges, a stark contrast to the freeform system in the early access period. While I understand the need to have a progression system to keep people playing, I do wonder if there was a more elegant way to do this. Beyond that, multiplayer is also a treat, the maps feel great to run around with friends with and the tag game mode in particular is a lot of fun. 

Overall this game truly captures the parkour training experience with a robust, in-depth system that keeps me coming back whenever I want to get into the flow and relax at the end of the day.

FINAL SCORE: 9/10

The game seemed fun and has some solid looking visuals to the trailer that got me into it, but this game seems to have missed the point of Free Running and Parkour being about momentum and flow. The game has an overly complicated system of button combos (hold this and tap that, tap this and flick that, Hold this tap that flick and then just before landing double tap that again. If you are mid combo on anything it will not flow into something else and must be completed or you ragdoll for no reason other than the combo was not completed) that are needed to do basic actions that makes the game play more of a chore in remembering what to press and when than having fun running around and doing what the game is intended for. It also fails to explain that some actions are not able to be performed while holding sprint, and that the obstacles you encounter have an overriding affect on the tricks you try to do. There is such a precise timing needed to do aerial tricks over half-walls you will end up vaulting them due to the combo of buttons to do the aerial trick is the same as the vaulting trick minus one. It took very little time for me to realize this game was not about flow, and more about frame timing and sequence memorization when I tried to just have my character do some jump steps up some boxes and he couldn't even do that without having to do some kind of combo tricks to get up two stacks of boxes. If you are into frame timing and tekken/street-fighter button combos go ahead you will really like this game, if you are looking to just run around and jump about Mirrors Edge games are much easier to figure out and control.

I want to love this, I really do. It's got all the makings of a relaxing low stakes trick game. The controls in theory are well adjusted to the type of game this is and allow for flexibility and player expression, but some bugs and quirks really hold it back. For instance, when certain conditions your buttons will behave different to how they normally do. Your held jump button will sometimes decide that you are intending to do a stunt, forcing you into a trick you don't have the clearance for. On a few occasions when trying to do a running jump from the end of a thin wall it would catapult me into a dive straight to the ground when I was trying to gain more height. There are also some key moves missing. The lack of any sort of wall kick really sticks out, but the wall running and wall climbing mechanics in general are very stiff and rudimentary. Moves requiring multiple held buttons and triggers can often feel stiff and occasionally unreliable, and any moves requiring specific set ups of map geometry like striding and power leaping feel railroaded.

I don't envy the movement system dev. Their task is difficult and I am sure they will improve the flow of the game over time, but in the meantime this doesn't satisfy my parkour itches. Before I go I will say that the area this game shines most is trick lines. If you can take the time to understand the quirks of the movement system and plan out your routes in ways that compliment its strengths and mitigate its weaknesses you can build a line that you can explore with a decent variety of stunts to choose from. But for me, the game just doesn't quite capture that free flowing fantasy.

I wish I could recommend this game, it has a lot of charm and potential, but it still feels like an early access game, not only in bugs/flaws but features and design. As such, charging $25 USD is way too much. I could probably recommend it at half the price. For this review, I've dabbled in all of the levels and got Gold on every challenge in one of the levels (Which the gold medals in this game feel tough to meet, only ever beating time trials by milliseconds or 1-2 seconds at most), so I feel like I've played with the mechanics and systems enough to have a solid opinion.

The biggest flaw has to be the controls (It was designed for controller, so will be referencing their inputs), well specifically how you do tricks. It feels like it was ripped straight from other trick systems (Tony Hawks, SSX, etc ), you do them by being airborne, holding the North/South/West face buttons and flicking your left stick in one of the four directions. This is great for those other games where you have long hang times and can freestyle moves and chain them together before you hit the ground, but as a parkour game, you hardly have the opportunity to string moves together more than 2 at a time, if even that. What's worse, and the main reason I bring this up, is that the jump button (south face button) has one too. This game also feature variable jumping where holding the button increases distance. So often times, as I've seen in other reviews or gameplay, you will try to prep a jump by holding it just before you land, but if you press the jump button while in air, you do a trick and flail out and crash. And because it's tied in with left stick, there is often conflict between movement and tricking (Better make sure your stick returns to neutral before trying to trick). Maybe a combo system would have been better here, or trick on button release instead of press, or just not using the jump button as also a trick button (And you can't remap controls, so that's great for a fully released game in 2025).

Besides the core problem, there are a lot of minor gripes that indicate it should still be in early access, like your characters arms and legs and the camera clipping through walls and seeing inside textures. The tutorial being very bare bones and feeling like devolopment test world, and then you having to spend the next 20 mins in the menu's learning things the tutorial left out (which is a lot). There's also some inconsistencies with the zipline, both in how it functions and compared to other systems (You hold to hang zipline but not for ledges? I thought back ejects were just straight up broken until I stopped holding the button, but don't expect side ejects if you're an AC fan). Some of the environments feel very barren, flat textured walls, no ornamentation (don't expect to be hopping up window shutters or electrical boxes) though I will say the parkour gym is really nice. I also wish there was more feedback. How long am I or can I hold the jump button? Do I have enough speed to wall run? Contextual prompts would be nice, like if I hold left shoulder button, the UI should display my options instead of burying it in a menu.

Now for features, there are 6 maps each with 8 challenges. There are only 2 types of challenges, time trials (Run through rings), and trick rush (do tricks in a shrinking area for score). The medals will reward currency which can be used for cosmetics. That's the entire game. I really wish there was more variety, maybe a race to the goal any way possible, or maybe a single trick score, or maybe don't get caught by AI or run from a wall. You'd think there would be a ghost mode or something to guide players, or even better yet, design the levels so that the challenge teaches new concepts and becomes more difficult over time. The game does a horrible job teaching you anything. There is also adrenaline (boost) and the scoring system. The scoring system has a timing window that gets smaller the higher the combo. Adrenaline will pause the timing window, so at higher scores you are spam clicking Left Stick In, otherwise you'll randomly lose your combo, which does not feel fun at all.

There are multiplayer game modes, but they are half baked at best. There's capture the flag, trick rush, and tag. If you are tagged/flag holder your L1/LB standing jump is just lost and replaced with a tag, and there's an annoying push mechanic that is very inconsistent (again, contextual prompts would help). You cant even change map or communicate in the lobby before hand, and winning the matches gives no reward. The maps are way too big for the game modes of 4 players. I feel like the taggers name should be invisible and move faster or have faster filling adrenaline or something. There's a free play multiplayer mode that is nice if you don't have toxic players. 

The inputs are very tight, and the feet landing has to be perfect, there were so many times it looked like the character would land the move, just to trip (even mashing roll). I often felt more frustration than fun getting gold on the challenges.

Part of the negative review is that the game just isn't for me, doing the same time trial for 30 mins because I held jump a millisecond before I landed to prep my next long jump just to unlock a new shoe isn't my cup of tea. There's a lot of skill for this game, but also some luck and jank. And I know it's an Idie dev, and I would have recommended this if it was early access and cheaper, but it just feels and looks unpolished. Game has a ton of potential and is really fun at times. The soundtrack is great and you can tell a lot of love and passion went into this game, but ultimately it still needs some work. I hope the game continues to be improved.

[h1] 💬 Personal Take & Recommendation [/h1]

[h3] 🧠 Personal Take [/h3]  
I used to love the competitive side of this game. It felt fast, fluid, and chaotic in the best way. But then they started nerfing and removing mechanics left and right “to fix multiplayer,” even though the multiplayer scene was already practically dead.

They nerfed features because 3% of players abused them, but meanwhile the remaining 97% are stuck with a dumbed-down, barely-functional competitive experience. And don't get me started on how long it takes to unlock anything cosmetic-wise. Feather unlocks? Are we serious right now 😂

Tried it again mid-2025, and it’s not better—it’s *worse*. Feels more broken than before. Like someone tried to "clean up" the game by just deleting half the tools instead of fixing them.

But hey, if you're just looking to parkour around and do tricks solo? It's still pretty fun. Just don’t expect much from the multiplayer unless you’ve got a group of friends to squad up with.

This game had potential. It really did. But every update seems to dig it deeper into a hole of mediocrity. Instead of polishing what works and improving multiplayer, they’re just removing stuff that made the game unique—all to fix problems affecting a tiny fraction of the player base.

Until they actually start listening to the community and making meaningful improvements, *Roof Tops & Alley Ways* is only worth your time if you're flying solo and can ignore the mess.
